campaign_eta_projection.risk_not_captured: Per-unit cost under sustained 8-way contention on this MacBook Air M4 was not isolated against a width-1 control on the SAME spec, so the projection assumes the production 94.396 s/unit does not inflate under load. If it inflates by more than ~21% the 8-hour goal is at risk. Memory was not a limiter in the real arm.
campaign_eta_projection.status: PROJECTION - not a measured full-campaign result
campaign_eta_projection.stretch_goal_4_active_hours: NOT supported by this projection for a cold full campaign; it IS comfortably met for resuming the stopped campaign from its existing 1 083 cached units
campaign_eta_projection.sub_one_hour_claim: not made - no direct measurement supports it
campaign_eta_projection.why_projection: No cold full campaign was run; the stopped campaign was deliberately NOT restarted. The projection multiplies two separately measured quantities.

campaign_projection.basis: The frozen campaign measured cache_verify_seconds 0.207913 for 4 080 parent-facing lookups, i.e. ~51 microseconds per verified lookup. A fully cached 1 690-parent campaign performs 8 450 such lookups.
campaign_projection.caveat: This is extrapolation from a partially cached production workspace plus a fully cached synthetic one. A genuinely complete production cache does not exist yet, so the 30-minute target is not claimed as directly measured.
campaign_projection.projected_total_minutes: well under 30, dominated by enumeration and artifact publication rather than by cache reads

measured.result: zero units executed, zero SUMO, units_simulated == 0

fixture.note: Every arm replays the same seeded per-unit duration profile, so a wide arm cannot win by drawing cheaper units.

real_sumo_arm.command: run_monthly_closure_search.py --global-daily-queue --daily-workers 8 --seed-workers 1 --max-active-sumo-slots 8 on an isolated spec, workspace root and cache root
real_sumo_arm.purpose: The scheduler arms above replace SUMO with a sleeping stand-in. This arm runs the REAL pipeline end to end so the concurrency ceiling and the achieved width are measured against actual SUMO processes.

runner_telemetry_at_17_of_20_units.cache_misses_note: 0 is correct and not a contradiction: under the queue a parent legitimately hits the cache because the queue produced its units moments earlier. units_simulated is the count of real work.

real_sumo_arm.sampling_method: Process ancestry from the run's PID (full ps tree walk), not a grep over command lines - an early grep-based attempt was inflated by the agent's own command line and by the grep process itself.

shutdown_observation.finding: SIGTERM to the search PID ALONE let the parent exit while two in-flight isolated workers (and their SUMO children) kept running as orphans until they finished their unit on their own.
shutdown_observation.no_corruption: The orphans published nothing partial: publication is atomic and is the last step inside the per-content-key single-flight lock, and flock is released by the kernel on exit.
shutdown_observation.operational_rule: Signal the process GROUP, not the PID. The production campaign stop used SIGINT to process group 68201 and left nothing behind - zero workers, zero SUMO, zero caffeinate, lock released - because group delivery reaches the workers and their SUMO children too.
shutdown_observation.why: Each daily unit runs in its own subprocess. IndependentDailyRunner.cleanup() shuts the pool down with wait=True and does reap them, but only when cleanup actually runs; a signal that ends the parent first bypasses it. This is a property of the pre-existing isolated-worker design, not of the queue.

real_sumo_arm.spec_note: 2027-09-01..2027-09-20, five-day parents, 06:00-14:00 band. These units are EIGHT-HOUR closures and are therefore much cheaper than the production campaign's full-day (00:00-24:00) units. This arm measures CONCURRENCY, not per-unit cost.

tail_observation.finding: 17 of 20 units completed in 74.1 s wall (35.53 s worker time each). The final 3 units were far more expensive - individual SUMO invocations of 3-5 minutes each, with several run per unit.
tail_observation.interpretation: A minority of units is much costlier than the mean. This is a property of the units, not of the scheduler: the same units are equally slow on the legacy path, where they would run one at a time instead of overlapped. It is the reason the campaign ETA below is built from production's own 851-unit mean rather than from this small fixture.
